subject: Control geom_boxplot for cases with sample size n=1

messages.author: 6873525055e7cfa8
messages.subject: Control geom_boxplot for cases with sample size n=1
parts:
Dear ggplot2 experts!

I am using geom_boxplot and overplot it with geom_point to represent
the single data points that contribute to each box. However in case of
just a few datapoints, I would like to avoid plotting the box but just
plot the points with geom_point. Please see the following example in
which I would like to avoid the horizontal line on the left.

data <- mtcars[-which(mtcars$cyl==4)[2:length(which(mtcars$cyl==4))],]
p <- ggplot(data, aes(factor(cyl), mpg))
p + geom_boxplot() + geom_point()


Many thanks for your help!
J.

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Control geom_boxplot for cases with sample size n=1
parts: Maybe there's a better way, but I'd split the data according to the count as follows...

#make a backup
data1<-data

#Attach count data to dataframe:
require(plyr)
data2<-ddply(data, .(cyl), transform, count=length(cyl))

#Take only data which has more than 3 points
data2<-data2[which(data2$count>3),]


require(ggplot2)
ggplot()+
geom_boxplot(data=data2,aes(factor(cyl), mpg))+
geom_point(data=data1, aes(factor(cyl), mpg))

HTH, 

Brandon
